transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… I guess the main thing is work. I process insurance claims, and I’m supposed to be at my workstation going through reviews, but I keep getting up. Like, even when I know I need to stay there and finish them, I’ll just… stand up and walk away.

It’s been causing problems, or at least making the day harder. And the funny thing is, my desk is actually not bad—I have this chair I picked out because my old one was terrible, and I thought that would help, but it didn’t really. I’ll get up to grab water or check something, and then I’m not where I’m supposed to be.

So that’s kind of what pushed me to come in. I’m having trouble staying put long enough to get through my claim reviews.
When you’re sitting at your workstation, do you get an uncomfortable feeling in your legs that makes you need to move them or stand up?

Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I shift around in the chair sometimes, but I haven’t noticed like a leg feeling that forces me up or anything. It’s more like I’m just… up before I’ve really thought it through. Like I’ll notice the water cooler or remember something, and then I’m standing. But no, I don’t think it’s an uncomfortable leg thing.
When you get up from your workstation, do you feel like you have to do it to relieve a strong urge or to prevent something bad from happening?

No, I don’t think it’s like that. It’s not like if I don’t get up something bad will happen, or like some huge pressure I’m trying to relieve. It’s more just… I’m supposed to stay at my desk and finish the claim reviews, and somehow I keep getting up anyway.

Like I’ll start a batch, then I’m standing up for some reason, and then I’m behind again. That’s really the part that made me come in.
Have you had trouble sitting still or staying focused like this since you were a child?

Yeah… looking back, I don’t think this is totally new. I mean, I wasn’t like thinking about it that way as a kid, obviously, I was just trying to get through school and, you know, recess was more interesting than worksheets.

But in elementary school, teachers would write stuff like I was bright, but I lost worksheets, or missed instructions, or needed reminders to finish classwork. My mom used to keep some of those comments, actually—she had this folder with report cards and school pictures, and I remember hating school picture day for some reason, I always had the weirdest haircut.

But yeah, the school comments were kind of the same theme: capable, but not keeping track of things and needing a lot of nudges to finish.
Have you ever had a period of several days when you felt unusually energetic or wired and needed much less sleep than usual?

I’m not sure… I don’t think so? I mean, I’ve had times where I stayed up too late, like scrolling or trying to finish something, and then the next day I’m dragging. But “wired” for several days and not needing sleep… I don’t really know.

I guess when work gets busy I can get keyed up, but then I still feel tired. Like last open enrollment period, everyone was behind and the office snacks were terrible—sorry, that’s not really the point. No, I haven’t noticed anything like needing way less sleep and feeling unusually energetic for days.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

I don’t know… I mean, I worry about normal stuff, I guess? Like bills or whether I messed something up, but I don’t think I’m sitting around worrying about everything all the time.

Sometimes I’ll get stuck thinking about something small, but then I also get distracted by, like, completely random things—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying when there’s no actual problem. At least I haven’t really noticed that.

Symptoms cause occupational impairment.
